stock.name: Kiniksa Pharmaceuticals International, plc
stock.thesis: Ranked first among today's eligible candidates on revenue growth, trailing year, six-month return against spy, six-month return against its sector — revenue +58.9% over the trailing year, operating margin wider than a year ago, earnings fully backed by cash.

evidence.label: Earnings yield / free cash flow yield
evidence.period: trailing year against the reference close

stock.peerBasis: 42 candidates in SIC major group 28, compared on free cash flow yield, all from the same source and the same periods.

runnersUp.name: Fortinet, Inc.

runnersUp.name: NetApp, Inc.
runnersUp.why: its weakest signal was cash conversion (-0.58)

runnersUp.name: NVIDIA Corporation
runnersUp.why: its weakest signal was cash conversion (-1.39)

stock.counterargument: It is an expensive stock: 82.4× trailing earnings and a 2.8% free cash flow yield, so the growth is already in the price and one weak quarter would cost a lot. growth decelerated against the previous quarter, so the trend in the numbers is already turning.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +55.5%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $58.63 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 113 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 113 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-21.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-10-28) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: 5 simple ways to relieve the aches and pains of sitting at a desk all day
stories.excerpt: Sitting at a desk all day hurts. And it isn't good for us. Strategies to make it a little more comfortable, from eye muscle exercises to alleviate eye strain to a back pain-fighting body movement.
stories.lead:
Back pain, eye strain, sluggishness, shoulder aches, restlessness.

If you sit in front of a computer for long periods of time, whether it's for work or leisure, you've probably experienced one of these symptoms.

But there are ways to relieve some of this discomfort — and even combat some of the health risks that may come with prolonged sitting. That includes walking breaks, ergonomic solutions and quick, simple stretches.

stories.title: Some New Yorkers hail ban on horse-drawn carriages, but drivers fear for incomes
stories.excerpt: As councillors prepare to banish the vehicles, views in Central Park are divided over the 160-year-old tradition.
stories.lead:
After petting a carriage horse in New York's Central Park at the age of five, Alexus Lawson was hooked.

She has driven a carriage in Manhattan's most famous park, pulled by her horse, for six years. But since Lawson heard about the city's vote this week to outlaw the carriages over animal and public-safety concerns, she has been worried.

"What am I supposed to do with my horse?" asked the 28-year-old, who has been driving in the park for six years. "You're going to tell me I can't work with her anymore? How am I supposed to ensure her health?"

stories.title: Two European women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya
stories.excerpt: The aid workers from Switzerland and Austria are due to fly home on Thursday, reports say.
stories.lead:
Two women - a Swiss and an Austrian – have been freed after more than a year in captivity in Niger and handed over to authorities in the Libyan city of Benghazi.

Swiss national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Austrian Claudia Abbt, 69, were kidnapped separately in the northern Nigerien city of Agadez in January and April last year.

No details have been given about who was holding them or their demands, although some reports have previously linked the kidnapping to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of their release were not disclosed.

stories.title: How long does it take to save up for a starter home? Twice as long as it did in 2019
stories.excerpt: A new analysis finds that the average renter household now needs 16 years to save for a down payment and closing costs. Rising rents and other costs have consumed a growing share of household budgets.
stories.lead:
Mortgage rates topping 7% is the latest sign of how hard it has gotten to buy a first house, with aspiring owners already facing sky-high prices. A new analysis out Thursday shines a light on yet another growing obstacle: the amount needed to close a home loan.

"Over the last seven years, the time to save up that down payment and closing costs has doubled," said Mike Calhoun, president of the Center for Responsible Lending, a research nonprofit that promotes economic opportunity. The report was released by the center's Julian Bond Institute.

stories.title: Who is close to a yellow card suspension in Champions League?
stories.excerpt: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains what the rules are regarding yellow card suspensions in this season's Champions League
stories.lead:
Players will receive a one-match ban should they receive four yellow cards before the semi-finals of the Champions League.

This rule runs from the start of the league phase until the end of the quarter-finals. After then, all yellow cards are wiped out and players cannot be suspended for multiple yellow cards.

The same rules apply for both the Europa League and the Conference League.
